post_text:
I watched the project head toward a cliff and kept my hands in my pockets.

It was the hardest thing I did that year.

A new team member wanted to change how we handled our daily process.

I saw the flaw in his logic immediately.

My ego wanted to step in and fix the path before he tripped.

I wanted to be the hero who saved the week.

Instead, I stayed silent and let him own the outcome.

He spent three days struggling with the exact problem I anticipated.

I felt the urge to say "I told you so" every single morning. ✋

Then, on the fourth day, he didn't just fix the mistake.

He built a shortcut that I had completely overlooked for years.

If I had intervened, we would have stayed safe and mediocre.

By stepping back, I allowed him to fail and then outpace me.

True leadership isn't about being right.

It is about creating the space for others to be better than you. 🚀
lesson_extracted: Stepping back allows others to find solutions you are too experienced to see.
